arraybufferwriter-growing-buffer.title: Build variable-size output with ArrayBufferWriter
arraybufferwriter-growing-buffer.short: Grow an IBufferWriter-backed buffer without repeated manual resizing
arraybufferwriter-growing-buffer.summary: ArrayBufferWriter<T> provides a reusable growable buffer through the IBufferWriter<T> contract.
arraybufferwriter-growing-buffer.why: It is useful when the final encoded size is unknown but producers can write directly into spans instead of repeatedly allocating intermediate arrays.
arraybufferwriter-growing-buffer.tips: Always call Advance with exactly the number of initialized elements and use WrittenSpan or WrittenMemory only after writing is complete.

filesystemwatcher-event-coalescing.title: Treat FileSystemWatcher as a change signal, not a transaction log
filesystemwatcher-event-coalescing.short: Coalesce file events and verify the resulting filesystem state
filesystemwatcher-event-coalescing.summary: FileSystemWatcher reports operating-system file notifications whose timing and multiplicity can vary across platforms and editors.
filesystemwatcher-event-coalescing.why: A single logical save can produce several notifications, so consumers should queue and coalesce work rather than equate one event with one business operation.
filesystemwatcher-event-coalescing.tips: Keep handlers short, tolerate duplicate events, and re-read authoritative filesystem state after a suitable debounce interval.

filesystemwatcher-exactly-once-assumptio.title: Do not assume FileSystemWatcher delivers exactly one event per change
filesystemwatcher-exactly-once-assumptio.short: Design file monitoring to tolerate duplicates and missed intermediate states
filesystemwatcher-exactly-once-assumptio.summary: Filesystem notifications are not an exactly-once durable event stream and can be duplicated, combined, or overflow under pressure.
filesystemwatcher-exactly-once-assumptio.why: Running irreversible work directly for every notification can duplicate processing or act on a file before the writer has finished updating it.
filesystemwatcher-exactly-once-assumptio.tips: Use notifications to trigger reconciliation, debounce bursts, and make downstream processing idempotent where possible.

activitylistener-sampling.title: Control Activity collection with ActivityListener sampling
activitylistener-sampling.short: Select which Activity sources and payloads are recorded
activitylistener-sampling.summary: ActivityListener observes ActivitySource instances and decides through sampling callbacks whether activities and their data should be created.
activitylistener-sampling.why: Sampling keeps tracing useful while controlling the CPU, allocation, and export volume of high-throughput applications.
activitylistener-sampling.tips: Keep sampling callbacks cheap and align sampling policy with the tracing exporter so important parent-child relationships remain understandable.

http-version-policy-negotiation.title: Choose HTTP version negotiation deliberately with HttpVersionPolicy
http-version-policy-negotiation.short: Specify whether a request requires, prefers, or can upgrade its HTTP version
http-version-policy-negotiation.summary: HttpRequestMessage.VersionPolicy controls how the requested HTTP version participates in protocol negotiation.
http-version-policy-negotiation.why: Explicit policy makes HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 expectations visible and avoids accidental fallback or failure when servers and transports differ.
http-version-policy-negotiation.tips: Choose policy from actual compatibility requirements and measure protocol behavior rather than assuming a newer version is always faster.

safehandle-native-resource-ownership.title: Represent native resource ownership with SafeHandle
safehandle-native-resource-ownership.short: Put native handle release behind a reliable managed lifetime
safehandle-native-resource-ownership.summary: SafeHandle encapsulates an operating-system or native handle and centralizes the code that releases it.
safehandle-native-resource-ownership.why: It is safer than scattering raw IntPtr cleanup across success, exception, and finalization paths, especially around P/Invoke.
safehandle-native-resource-ownership.tips: Define invalid handle values correctly, make ReleaseHandle non-throwing, and avoid exposing raw handles longer than required.

iasyncenumerable-enumeratorcancellation.title: Forward await foreach cancellation with EnumeratorCancellation
iasyncenumerable-enumeratorcancellation.short: Bind WithCancellation tokens to an async iterator parameter
iasyncenumerable-enumeratorcancellation.summary: EnumeratorCancellationAttribute tells the compiler which CancellationToken parameter of an async iterator should receive enumeration cancellation.
iasyncenumerable-enumeratorcancellation.why: Without the intended token flow, callers can request cancellation while the iterator continues waiting on I/O or producing items.
iasyncenumerable-enumeratorcancellation.tips: Pass the token through every cancellable operation inside the iterator and keep cancellation behavior consistent with other async APIs.

aspnetcore-endpoint-filter-crosscutting.title: Use endpoint filters for focused Minimal API cross-cutting behavior
aspnetcore-endpoint-filter-crosscutting.short: Apply validation or endpoint-specific policy around Minimal API handlers
aspnetcore-endpoint-filter-crosscutting.summary: Endpoint filters wrap Minimal API handler execution and can inspect arguments, short-circuit a request, or process the result.
aspnetcore-endpoint-filter-crosscutting.why: They provide a focused place for endpoint-level concerns without duplicating validation or policy code in every handler.
aspnetcore-endpoint-filter-crosscutting.tips: Use middleware for broad pipeline concerns and filters when behavior depends on endpoint arguments or metadata.

threadpool-blocking-starvation.title: Do not hide blocking async work inside Task.Run on server hot paths
threadpool-blocking-starvation.short: Await naturally asynchronous I/O instead of occupying ThreadPool workers
threadpool-blocking-starvation.summary: Wrapping synchronous waits on asynchronous I/O in Task.Run still blocks a worker and can amplify ThreadPool starvation under load.
threadpool-blocking-starvation.why: As concurrency rises, blocked workers delay queued continuations and requests, increasing latency even though the code appears asynchronous.
threadpool-blocking-starvation.tips: Keep the call chain async end to end; isolate genuinely blocking legacy work only when its concurrency is deliberately bounded.

weakreference-cache-semantics.title: Understand WeakReference before using it as a cache
weakreference-cache-semantics.short: Allow GC to reclaim a target without treating it as deterministic eviction
weakreference-cache-semantics.summary: WeakReference<T> does not keep its target alive, so the target can disappear whenever no strong references remain and GC collects it.
weakreference-cache-semantics.why: This can reduce retention for recreatable objects, but it does not provide cache capacity, expiration, or predictable hit behavior.
weakreference-cache-semantics.tips: Use a real cache when policy matters and reserve weak references for semantics where opportunistic survival is acceptable.
